question.text: What will the month-over-month change in US producer prices excluding food, energy, and trade services be for October 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves based on the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics' Producer Price Index news release for October 2026, scheduled for publication at 8:30 a.m. ET on Friday, November 13, 2026 (https://www.bls.gov/news.release/ppi.nr0.htm). The answered value is the seasonally adjusted 1-month percent change reported for the index for "final demand less foods, energy, and trade services" — the figure stated in the release narrative, e.g. "prices for final demand less foods, energy, and trade services moved up 0.5 percent in September." A reported decrease of 0.1 percent resolves as -0.1, and "unchanged" resolves as 0. The value as first published is used; later revisions do not change the resolution.
question.fine_print: If the October 2026 release is delayed, the question resolves when the October 2026 figures are first published. If the October 2026 figures have not been published by February 28, 2027, or if the BLS skips the October 2026 release entirely, the question is annulled.

research:

## 1. Resolution source

July is now 0.5, revised from the 0.4 in the question's background. [BLS archive](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/ppi_10152026.htm)
- 2026-10-15: Other September details from the same release:
  - Services less trade, transportation and warehousing: +0.3% (Aug 0.0, Jul 0.7, Jun 0.2, May 0.7).
  - Core goods (goods less foods and energy): +0.3%.
  - Securities brokerage and investment advice fell.
  - May to August data were revised. [BLS archive](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/ppi_10152026.htm)
- Note: the code's statistical baseline uses FRED WPSFD4131 (finished goods less foods and energy). That is a different series from the one this question resolves on, so its percentiles (median about 0.22) will run low.

## 2. Current status

## 4. Base rates
- Last 12 months (Oct 2025 to Sep 2026): mean about 0.42%, median 0.5%, range 0.1 to 0.8. Five of 12 readings were 0.5, two were 0.3, and three were at or below 0.2 (0.1, 0.2, 0.2).
- Last 6 months: 0.5, 0.8, 0.2, 0.5, 0.3, 0.5, with no clear trend.
- October 2025 read 0.6.
- The 12-month rate is 5.0%, which works out to roughly 0.4% a month on average.
- Month-to-month swings run about ±0.3 percentage points. Revisions of 0.1 between releases are common.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no consensus for this exact series. The Trading Economics and Investing.com calendars show it blank for the November 13 release. [TradingEconomics](https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/ppi-ex-food-energy-and-trade-services-mom), [Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/economic-calendar/united-states-producer-price-index-(ppi)-mom-238)
- Kalshi "PPI MoM October": this is the headline final demand index, not this series. Its prices imply roughly a 63% chance of headline above 0.5%, 81% above 0.2%, and 12% above 1.1%. The ladder is not internally consistent: "above 0.6%" trades at 0.61, close to "above 0.5%" at 0.63.
- Kalshi PPI YoY (headline): about 50% for above 6.5%.
- Polymarket PPI YoY: the low buckets (6.4% and under) are all priced at 4% or less. That points to expectations above 6.4%, but the market looks thin.
- Kalshi core CPI October: the mode is 0.2% (43%), then 0.3% (39%).

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- The October CPI release date is not confirmed in what I found. It is normally around November 10 to 13, and the Kalshi market for it is live.
- 2026-11-04: ISM services, including its prices component.
- Weekly EIA diesel prices and freight indices.
- Possible government data delays: the fine print allows publication up to February 28, 2027.
- 2026-11-13, 8:30 ET: the October PPI release, which will also revise August and September.

I've finished the research and am writing it up now. The short version: October's figure isn't out yet, and I found no economist forecast or prediction market for this exact series. All nine 2026 readings fell between +0.2% and +0.8%.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-03: The BLS release page (ppi.nr0.htm) and the DOL PDF both returned HTTP 403 to the raw-data tool, so I couldn't read the live page directly. [BLS](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/ppi.nr0.htm)
- 2026-10-15 (the archived September release): final demand less foods, energy, and trade services rose **+0.5%** in September, after +0.3% in August. It was up 5.0% over 12 months. Trading Economics shows the index at 144.26, up from 143.56. [BLS archive](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/ppi_10152026.htm), [Trading Economics](https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/core-producer-prices-mom)
- Other September detail:
  - Final demand services: +0.8%.
  - Trade services: +1.4%.
  - Transportation and warehousing: +3.4%.
  - Services less trade, transportation and warehousing: +0.3%. Securities brokerage, dealing and investment advice fell.
  - Goods less foods and energy: +0.3% (+5.1% over 12 months).
  - Earlier stages of production rose sharply: Stage 1 +2.2%, Stage 2 +3.9%, Stage 3 +1.1%, Stage 4 +1.1%. [BLS archive](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/ppi_10152026.htm)
- The supplied statistical baseline uses the wrong series. FRED WPSFD4131 is "finished goods less foods and energy", not "final demand less foods, energy, and trade services", so its percentiles (median about 0.22) should be used with caution.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The October figures come out 2026-11-13 at 8:30 ET. [BLS schedule](https://www.bls.gov/schedule/news_release/ppi.htm)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-02/03: The ISM manufacturing index rose to 55.5 in October from 54.5, its tenth straight month of growth. Production grew at its fastest pace since November 2021. S&P Global's manufacturing index was 54.9, and coverage mentions supply and price pressures. I couldn't find the October ISM prices index. That matters for transportation services, which are included in this measure. [Al-Masry Al-Youm](https://www.almasryalyoum.com/news/details/4398555)

## 4. Base rates
- 2026 monthly readings as shown in the September release (some include revisions): Jan 0.5, Feb 0.5, Mar 0.2, Apr 0.5, May 0.8, Jun 0.2, Jul 0.5, Aug 0.3, Sep 0.5. [BLS archive](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/ppi_10152026.htm)
  - Average about 0.44, median 0.5, range 0.2 to 0.8.
  - 7 of 9 months were at or above 0.3. None were 0.1 or lower.
  - July was first reported as 0.4 and now shows 0.5, so the first print can differ from the revised figure.
- 12-month change: 4.8% in August, 5.0% in September, so the trend is still rising.
- Possible headwind: transportation and warehousing jumped 3.4% in September, which could partly reverse. Possible tailwind: early-stage production prices are rising fast (Stage 2 up 13.9% over 12 months).

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no consensus forecast for October core PPI. Investing.com, Forex Factory and Trading Economics all list it as blank so far. [Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/economic-calendar/united-states-core-producer-price-index-(ppi)-mom-62), [Forex Factory](https://www.forexfactory.com/calendar/87-us-core-ppi-mm)
- The Kalshi market "PPI MoM in October" is almost certainly **headline** final demand, not this series. Its prices: above 0.2%: 0.81, above 0.3%: 0.76, above 0.4%: 0.68, above 0.5%: 0.63, above 0.7%: 0.58, above 1.1%: 0.12. That implies a headline median around 0.7-0.8%, though the ladder isn't entirely consistent.
- Kalshi PPI year-over-year: about 0.55 for above 6.5%, implying a headline median near 6.5-6.6%. Polymarket's year-over-year market looks illiquid or mispriced, with every bucket at about 3%.
- Kalshi October core CPI: the most likely outcomes are 0.2% (0.43) and 0.3% (0.39).
- I found no market for "final demand less foods, energy, and trade services" specifically.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- About 2026-11-05: ISM services report, including its prices index (date not confirmed).
- About 2026-11-10 to 11-12: October CPI release (date not confirmed). Some of its components, such as airfares, feed into PPI.
- Economists' consensus forecasts should appear on calendars during the week of Nov 9.
- Watch for oil, diesel and freight moves and any tariff news. October's Middle East and Hormuz disruption kept crude near or above $100.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left:** The October 2026 PPI is released on November 13, 2026, about 10 days from now.

(b) **Latest known value:** Final demand less foods, energy and trade services rose 0.5% month over month (seasonally adjusted) in September 2026, published October 15, 2026. July was revised to 0.5% and August was 0.3%.

(c) **If nothing changed:** The October print would be 0.5%.

(d) **If the trend continued:** The last 12 months averaged about 0.42% (median 0.5%), and the 5.0% annual rate implies roughly 0.4% a month. That puts the trend at about 0.4 to 0.5%.

(e) **Historical variation:** Single months swing about ±0.3 percentage points around the trend. Over the past year the range was 0.1 to 0.8, and in earlier years single-month moves were sometimes larger.

(f) **Expectations of experts and markets:**
- There is no consensus forecast for this series.
- Kalshi's market on headline PPI puts a 63% chance on a reading above 0.5%, which points to inflation pressure staying hot.
- The ISM manufacturing prices index eased only slightly, to 75.2 from 77.9.
- Crude is still very high (Brent around $117), which supports transportation and warehousing costs.
- The FRED baseline in the research is a different series (finished goods less foods and energy) and runs low, so I do not anchor on it.

(g) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- **Low:** Transportation and warehousing reverses part of September's 3.4% spike, and portfolio management fees fall with equity markets. That could produce a reading of about 0.0 to 0.1, or even slightly negative.
- **High:** Diesel and freight pass-through broadens, tariff effects spread across machinery and equipment, and investment-advice fees jump. That could push the reading to 0.9 to 1.1 or more.

**Tail cases:**
- **1st percentile:** A broad services reversal plus a fall in portfolio management fees gives about -0.2.
- **99th percentile:** A surge in energy-driven transport plus services gives about 1.2.
